I'm Nicole Gordon, and I'm deeply honored to step into

the role of Club Manager for Terrace Club. It's a significant
moment for me, as I'm proud to be the first woman to hold
this position in the club's history. My background in the service
industry has instilled a deep passion for serving and enriching
community experiences. At Terrace, my vision is to cultivate
an even stronger sense of belonging, transforming the club
into a vibrant home where art, food, and music not only
converge but truly flourish. I'm excited to work alongside our
members and alumni to enhance this incredible legacy for
every Terran.

Ashley Blair brings strategy, sparkle, and spreadsheets
together in perfect harmony. With a strong foundation in
operations, HR, accounting, fundraising, and event planning,
she's helped organizations boost enrollment, secure hundreds
of thousands in donations, and transition seamlessly into
remote operations. Whether she’s coordinating fundraising
events, or planning closing out the fiscal year, Ashley brings

a detail oriented mindset and a warm, human touch. Her
experience spans schools, healthcare, and nonprofit sectors—
always with an eye for growth and meaningful impact. If you
need someone who can wear all the hats and still throw a great
event, she’s your person.

Hi Terrans,

I'm looking forward to my 17th year on the
Terrace board, and I keep serving each year
because of all the things that have never
changed -- and all the things that have changed.
I joined Terrace as a member because it was

the only place on campus to get a decent vegetarian entree
at every meal. All these years later, I'm still a vegetarian,
and Terrace still has the best options for everyone with a
meatless diet.

¥ Iwanted to be in a community where everyone could be
included no matter who they are. Today Terrace is still the
best place on or off the Princeton campus to come as you
are, and be welcomed.

I remember fondly -- though fuzzily -- Wednesday beer

nights, Friday members’ nights, and quiet afternoons sitting >
on the lawn in May. Now every new class of Terrans has added gg
its own traditions to the old.

In short Terrace balances the best of the past and the
future, future, future. So it's no wonder that the Club has
been more popular than any of those places on Prospect for
the last decade.

If you have memories of Terrace or ideas to share, please
reach out anytime to me at steve.feyer@terracefclub.org.

All the food,

What's the most Terrace memory you can share publicly?
You never want to see a groundhog INSIDE the house, as I

did in the summer of 2009. While our encounter with the king
of the backyard was harrowing, we managed to get him back
out of the house in a humane fashion by chasing him into the
servery, closing the doors, and assembling a chute to the side
door with our dining room tables, so he had only one path of
escape. It went much better for him than certain unfortunate
salmon, goldfish, or crickets that attended Dare to Care over
the years.

Family Visit to the Club

This past summer, a family with adult children stopped by the club while it
was closed for renovations. One of the workers let us know about your visit
afterward.

We heard that your father, a former officer or staff member, had passed
away and you were hoping to get a picture inside his old haunt. For so
many of us, this place holds layers of memory, andknowing you all wished
to return, even just for a photograph, touched us greatly. The club carries
pieces of all wha have been part of its story, and his presence here is very
much a part of that history.

You mentioned traveling from out of town, and we regret we missed the
chance to connect while you were here.

If this was your family, please reach out. We would be honored to connect
with you and remember him together.

RICE SALAD, BARCELONA STYLE

10 servings

Salad 1/4 teaspoon dried tarragon, crushed

2 tablespoons olive oll 2 green onions, minced =
1/4 cup minced onion 1 dill pickle, minced F
1 medium clove garlic, peeled and minced 1 medium green bell pepper, seeded and

11/2 cups white rice minced

11/2 cups chicken broth 1/2 medium carrot, peeled and minced 3
11/2 cups water 1/2 medium cucumber, peeled and minced |
1/4 teaspoon salt 3 small romaine leaves (from the inner part of {3
1 sprig parsley the head)

1/4 teaspoon dried thyme, crushed 1 whole canned pimento, diced

Dressing 1/4 teaspoon dried thyme

4 tablespoons olive oil 1 medium clove garlic, peeled and forced

3 tablespoons lemon juice through a press

1 tablespoon red-wine vinegar 1/4 teaspoon salt

1 teaspoon Dijon mustard Freshly ground black pepper to taste

1. To prepare the salad: In a medium pan heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add
the onion and garlic, sauteing until softened. Add the rice and stir to coat. Add
the chicken broth, water, salt, parsley, thyme and tarragon. Bring to a boil and
continue to boil until the level of the water just covers the rice. Cover, turn the
heat to low and cook 20 minutes. Remove from the heat and cool slightly.

2. To prepare the dressing: In a small jar combine the olive oil, lemon juice, red-
wine vinegar, mustard, thyme, garlic, salt and pepper. Shake well until emulsified.

3. Pour the dressing over the rice. Add green onions, pickle, bell pepper, carrot,
cucumber, romaine and pimento. Refrigerate, covered. Bring to room tempera-
ture 1 hour before serving. Adjust the seasonings if necessary.

We're in the dog days of summer, babies — and that means I'm running through all of my best
summer recipes before the season ends. This one is a classic - a favorite in my family for
generations and a staple of my seasonal cuisine. It comes together quickly and with very little
effort — pair it with a nice green salad for a perfect late-summer dinner.

Jenny Marlowe '04

CHEESE-TOMATO TARTE PROVENGALE

Ingredients 1/8 tsp pepper

1 pie crust, homemade or store-bought 1 tsp basil

3 cups Swiss cheese, shredded 1 tsp oregano

1/2 cup cheddar cheese, shredded 1/2 cup scallions, chopped
3 tomatoes 2 tbsp unsalted butter
1/2 tsp salt 2 tbsp breadcrumbs

1. Prepare pie crust according to your favorite recipe; or use a store-bought
pie shell — I for one will not judge you!

2. If you've made your own crust, roll it out and fit it into a 9” pie plate; trim any
overhang and crimp the edges.

3. Prick your pie shell all over with a fork; line with a double layer of aluminum foil
and fill with pie weights. Pre-bake your pie crust in a hot oven until golden (400°
for 12-15 minutes or according to package directions); set aside to cool and
reduce the oven temperature to 325°.

4. Mix the Swiss and cheddar cheeses and spoon them into your pie crust.

5. Slice the tomatoes in half lengthwise and then into thin wedges. Arrange
them in a circular pattern around the edge of the tart, slightly overlapping the
wedges.

6. Sprinkle the salt, pepper, basil, and oregano over the tomatoes.

7. Melt the butter in a small saucepan; sauté the scallions for a few minutes until
tender.

8. Spoon the scallions into the center of the tart; top with the breadcrumbs.

9. Bake at 325° for 20 minutes. Let the tart cool before slicing and serving.

Et voila, babies — you can feel trés francais as you enjoy this late-summer treat.
Bon appétit!
Jenny Marlowe's Cheese-Tomato Tarte Provencale
